title: Sparrow Networks — Renewal & APAC Edge Request
summary: Check-in ahead of renewal. Customer requested APAC edge capacity and private VPC options for data residency. Discussed options: Dedicated vs Private, latency SLOs, KMS/HSM for keys, proposed staged uplift and pilot in Singapore. Agreed next steps: provide APAC pricing sheet, security doc pack, and schedule on-prem/priv pilot scoping with SE. Action items assigned.
topics: private VPC vs Dedicated pool tradeoffs
next_steps: Jordan to send APAC pricing sheet and committed capacity options by 2025-03-18
Priya to share private deployment checklist and security pack (SOC2/ISO excerpts) by 2025-03-20
Schedule pilot scoping workshop w/ Sparrow infra and SRE — target week of 2025-03-31
action_items: Ethan Cole: Share current throughput & p99 latency dashboards (link) by 2025-03-17
Jordan Miles: Draft contract extension term options (6/12/24 month) and compute burst terms by 2025-03-18
Priya Shah: Prepare pilot runbook and perf test plan (includes seq len, qps, KV cache hints) by 2025-03-20
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Miles, Priya Shah, Liam Ortiz (Redwood); Ethan Cole, Maya Lin, Raul Gomez, Sofia Park (Sparrow)

[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for joining uh on a Friday afternoon, appreciate you making time. quick agenda: renewal terms, APAC edge ask, private/VPC options and follow ups.
[00:28] Ethan Cole: thanks jordan, yeah we wanted to get in front of renewal and a specific ask from product — they want APAC edge capacity in SG, and also tighter controls for keys. we ve been running mostly in us-west and eu-central and the latency for certain markets there is, uh, borderline.
[00:45] Maya Lin: just to add, timeline is Q2 renewal, we d like to lock terms before end of april if possible. also compliance team is picky about key management, they'd prefer KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for everything.
[01:05] Priya Shah: totally makes sense. quick question — are you thinking private deployment in APAC or Redwood dedicated pool in our hosted offering? the tradeoffs are different: private gives you VPC, complete control for residency; dedicated is faster to spin up and still keeps data behind our tenancy but not customer-managed networking.
[01:33] Raul Gomez: hm so we're leaning toward private for data residency. but we re open to a staged approach like dedicated first then private if the compliance audit requires it.
[01:44] Jordan Miles: that's a common pattern. we can propose a staged path: initial dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) for immediate latency improvement, with a parallel project to scope private VPC deployment — that keeps you live while we do the heavier lift.
[02:10] Sofia Park: for the dedicated option, how do you handle failover and region routing? if SG goes flaky, can you route to eu or us without big model deltas?
[02:28] Priya Shah: yes, smart routing lets us fallback to compatible model variant and region. latency will increase but availability remains. we also support model pinning per route so you can keep behaviour consistent.
[02:45] Ethan Cole: cost vs latency — product is sensitive to cost. how much of a delta are we looking at for dedicated vs private?
[02:59] Liam Ortiz: short answer, private has higher one-time infra/setup and slightly higher sustained cost due to isolation; dedicated is more predictable per-token pricing and lower infra ops from our side. we ll put numbers in the APAC pricing sheet.
[03:20] Maya Lin: ok, re: keys — does private support our KMS/HSM? we use an external HSM.
[03:31] Priya Shah: yes, private can integrate with customer KMS via peered connections; HSM integration will need coordination with security and a short engineering window for key wrapping and attestation steps. we'll include the checklist in the security pack.
[04:00] Raul Gomez: what's the SLA on latency? we 're targeting sub-60ms p50 for certain bursty inference endpoints.
[04:12] Priya Shah: for inference p50 under 60ms depends on model family and instance profile. if you pick a smaller transformer variant or quantized profile and we pin a low-seq path, it's achievable. p99 will be higher; we can set SLO tiers and automated fallback to cheaper region-model combos for overload.
[04:40] Ethan Cole: we'd want a few concrete benchmark runs — can Redwood run a perf test with our sample prompts in SG to validate numbers?
[04:52] Jordan Miles: yes, that's standard. priya can scope a perf test plan: sample prompt set, seq lengths, and QPS targets. we'll run in dedicated test pool in ap-southeast-1.
[05:10] Maya Lin: also procurement — any changes to contract language for private? we usually need data flow diagrams and liability language.
[05:23] Jordan Miles: understood. liam will surface contract addenda for private deployments and typical SOC2 attestation excerpts.
[05:35] Liam Ortiz: i'll also share our standard AUP and a few example addenda customers use for on-prem/private.
[05:44] Ethan Cole: competitor note — one of our teams piloted NimbusAI and they had similar edge promises but the routing/fallback was more manual. we're evaluating.
[05:58] Priya Shah: we've seen that; our smart routing and KV cache sharing across pools aims to reduce warm-start latency during failovers.
[06:15] Maya Lin: what about billing — can we have committed usage tiers and burst overage buckets?
[06:26] Jordan Miles: yes, we offer reserved capacity tiers and burst capacity options. you can commit to a base capacity for predictable pricing and allow bursts at a pre-agreed uplift rate.
[06:40] Raul Gomez: ok good. for the pilot, we also need logs to ship to our SIEM and audit trails retained for 12 months.
[06:50] Priya Shah: audit logs and delivery to external SIEM are supported for private; for hosted dedicated we'll provide export hooks and retention controls — we'll confirm retention windows in the security pack.
[07:10] Ethan Cole: timeline recap — we re renewing in Q2, want to start pilot in apac asap after terms. can you propose a plan and cost by mid-march?
[07:21] Jordan Miles: absolutely — i'll get the APAC pricing and term options over by tuesday 2025-03-18.
[07:30] Maya Lin: who from Redwood will lead the pilot scoping? we want an SE working with our infra to define network diagrams and perf targets.
[07:40] Priya Shah: i'll lead pilot scoping and liam will support contract ops. we ll propose a workshop w/ your infra and SRE.
[07:52] Sofia Park: sample data — for perf we'd prefer to use sanitized traces; can we share a small sample?
[08:02] Ethan Cole: yes i'll push sanitized traces to the folder.
[08:10] Jordan Miles: great thanks. any blockers?
[08:16] Maya Lin: one vendor question — our security team asked for proof of vulnerability scanning and segrego testing for the runtime images.
[08:27] Priya Shah: we do runtime scanning and periodic pentests; i'll include a summary and a contact in the security pack. note: some tooling names might be different in our docs but we'll include the findings summary.
[08:45] Raul Gomez: about model variants — if we use quantized model in SG and higher-precision in eu, any quality regression testing?
[08:56] Priya Shah: yes we can run evals tied to your golden prompt set and produce quality metrics so product can approve the quantized profiles. that's part of Optimize offering but SEs can run a focused eval for the pilot.
[09:20] Jordan Miles: ok let's capture next steps — i've noted Jordan send pricing, priya security pack and runbook, ethan supply dashboards and traces, and schedule scoping workshop.
[09:34] Maya Lin: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:40] Jordan Miles: thanks all, we 'll follow up with calendar invites.

[END] Note: transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions and overlapping talk; names sometimes tagged generically in the meeting export. Links referenced: APAC pricing sheet (to be sent), security pack (shared drive link), sanitized traces folder (customer to drop).
